text:
Detroit and Seattle meet for the second time in 11 days, and the Red Wings arrive with some payback in mind after losing 6-3 to the Kraken on Oct. 9. DET won its last game 4-3 in a shootout against San Jose after trailing by two goals, though it is without J.T. Compher, Mason Appleton and Marco Kasper. SEA is coming off an 8-3 loss at Florida and is missing Jacob Melanson and Ryan Lindgren, though Brandon Montour could return after coming off the out list.

The underlying play favors Detroit. At five on five, DET has taken 52% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) against SEA's 45%. Seattle's results are running ahead of its chances, with finishing doing most of the work. DET's power play also generates more expected goals per game than SEA's, though the Red Wings take 4.75 penalties a game. Projected goalies: Daniil Tarasov (DET) has saved 5.4 goals above expected over three games, while Philipp Grubauer (SEA) is at +4.06. Tarasov was at -2.84 last season to Grubauer's +5.35.

Alex DeBrincat, one goal from 300 for his career, is given a 41% chance to score. Lucas Raymond has gone eight games without a goal on 2.9 expected, so he's due. For Ice Sheet's under-the-radar pick, watch Michael Brandsegg-Nygård, a third-liner with 3.6 expected goals in his last eight games and a 21% chance to score.
